req.title: Reject player with duplicate squadNumber
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 409 Conflict when the squadNumber in a new player already belongs to another player.

doc.reasoning: R-PLAYER-008 requires HTTP 409 Conflict when a POST /players/ request carries a squadNumber already owned by an existing player. Three complementary tests are needed: (1) a positive case confirming a brand-new squadNumber is accepted with HTTP 201; (2) a negative/EP case confirming an exact duplicate squadNumber returns HTTP 409 with the correct detail message; (3) a boundary/STC case that first creates a player with a fresh squadNumber, then immediately retries the identical payload to confirm the transition from 'not-exists' to 'exists' triggers 409. Together these cover the comparison branch `if existing:` in player_route.post_async, the exact HTTP status constant HTTP_409_CONFLICT, and the detail string, killing status-code mutation, boolean-negation mutation, and constant-swap mutation operators.

tests.name: test_post_player_unique_squad_number_returns_201
preconditions: Database is pre-loaded with 26 rows; squadNumbers 1-26 are taken.
squadNumber 99 does not exist in the database.
actions: POST /players/ with a valid payload using squadNumber=99 (not in pre-loaded data).
expected: Response body contains the created player with squadNumber=99
Response body contains all submitted fields
trace: R-PLAYER-008: happy-path — unique squadNumber must succeed with 201, not 409
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_post_player_unique_squad_number_returns_201():
    payload = {
        "firstName": "Test",
        "lastName": "Player",
        "squadNumber": 99,
        "position": "Goalkeeper"
    }
    r = client.post("/players/", json=payload)
    assert r.status_code == 201
    body = r.json()
    assert body["squadNumber"] == 99
    assert body["firstName"] == "Test"
    assert body["lastName"] == "Player"
    assert body["position"] == "Goalkeeper"
    assert "id" in body

test_post_player_unique_squad_number_returns_201()

tests.name: test_post_player_second_post_same_squad_number_transitions_to_409
preconditions: squadNumber=50 does not exist in the database.
actions: POST /players/ with squadNumber=50 — first request (state: not-exists → created).
POST /players/ with squadNumber=50 again — second request (state: exists → conflict).
expected: First POST returns HTTP 201 Created with squadNumber=50 in body
Second POST body detail equals 'A Player with this squad number already exists.'
trace: R-PLAYER-008: state transition — system must move from accepting to rejecting once the squadNumber is registered; catches boolean-negation and status-code constant mutations

tests.name: test_post_player_duplicate_does_not_return_201
preconditions: squadNumber=5 already belongs to Vivaan Nair.
actions: POST /players/ with squadNumber=5 and different name/position fields.
Assert status code is exactly 409, not 200, not 201, not 422.
expected: Response body detail is the exact conflict message
trace: R-PLAYER-008: DT — decision table row: squadNumber exists=true → must return 409, never 2xx; catches status-code constant mutations (409->201, 409->200)
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_post_player_duplicate_does_not_return_201():
    payload = {
        "firstName": "Different",
        "lastName": "Name",
        "squadNumber": 5,
        "position": "Central Midfield",
        "team": "Some Team"
    }
    r = client.post("/players/", json=payload)
    assert r.status_code == 409
    assert r.status_code != 201
    assert r.status_code != 200
    assert r.status_code != 422
    body = r.json()
    assert body["detail"] == "A Player with this squad number already exists."
    assert "id" not in body

test_post_player_duplicate_does_not_return_201()
